answer: A farm that wants 113 keys as a result forfeits 113 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the ocean seed, the opal timing is verifiable from the prism record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 536 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is trivial once and expensive in bulk. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
